title: Scalar reduction in completed and section-ring coordinates
statement: Fix $P$ [def-pur-conventions] and simultaneous section-preserving coefficient models $D$ [def-sp-field-shriek-system-models]. Let $E\subset F$ be finite coefficient subfields and let $T$ be an arbitrary scheme. For any reduction towers $R_A,R_B$ over the coefficient-system coordinates of $D$ [det-sp-reduction-tower-normalized], there exist IntegralCoordinates and SystemCoordinates [def-sp-field-extension-integral-coordinates] [def-sp-field-extension-system-coordinates] identifying ordinary completed scalar extension with the section-ring scalar model and system scalar extension with the sequence-site model. These coordinates identify completed integral scalar extension with the same scalar model, and give an isomorphism of entire derived systems between reducing after integral scalar extension and extending the reduced system. These maps satisfy the two representative normalization equations of Reduction [def-sp-field-extension-reduction-limits], including multiplication on pure tensors and all quotient transitions.

proof.text:
identify each presented completed ring with the inverse limit of its finite
quotients by the coefficient projection equations. For the inclusion E to F the
map on sections is the inverse limit of the quotient inclusions. The two scalar
functors are identified on pure tensors by multiplication; the inverse inserts one.
Use these maps for IntegralCoordinates and conjugate by the section-preserving
system equivalences for SystemCoordinates. Finite-free completed comparison identifies
ordinary extension with integralScalarExtension on complete inputs. Composing its
inverse with the ordinary derived comparison gives integral; cancellation gives
integral_normalized. Apply reduction and compose with the multiplication comparison
of entire systems and the coordinate comparison. This gives reduction and exactly
reduction_normalized. Multiplication and insertion of one commute with each quotient
map on a single K-flat representative, so these are arrows of whole systems.

    (RB : SpReductionTower P.coefficients.l F.val T ((D.coordinates F).abelian T)) :
